summary: Dib Bangkok is a privately founded contemporary-art museum in a converted 1980s warehouse, with three floors of galleries, a substantial courtyard and a changing programme. For December 2026, the current exhibition is Giving Life (26 September 2026–3 May 2027), featuring more than 160 works by 33 Thai and international artists, including Alexander Calder; its Chanel Gateway Commission includes Nawin Nuthong’s interactive Project 147.
whyGo: See major Thai and international contemporary art in an architecturally distinctive, adaptive-reuse building.
The courtyard and galleries make the visit as much about space and light as individual artworks.
The scheduled December show offers kinetic sculpture and an interactive game-based commission alongside varied work.
bestFor: Visitors interested in Thai artists in an international collection
skipIf: You need a low-cost attraction: standard admission is THB 700.
You cannot manage a walk of roughly 18–20 minutes from BTS Ekkamai and have not arranged a ride.
You need child gallery access for a child under seven; the museum excludes under-sevens from galleries.
duration: Allow about 2–3 hours as a planning estimate for the galleries and courtyard; time needed varies with exhibition interest.
cost: Current official main-exhibition rates: THB 700 general admission, THB 550 Thai resident, THB 150 student ages 7–18, THB 250 student ages 19–22, THB 150 visitor with disability. Verify eligibility and rates before booking. James Turrell’s Straight Up Sunset Light Program is separately ticketed.
hours: Thursday–Tuesday, 10:00–19:00; closed Wednesday. Main galleries close 15 minutes before closing. The official plan-your-visit page is the current reference; check it again near your date for holiday changes.
bestTime: Go near opening for a quieter start, or book the separately ticketed sunset light programme if available and desired. December is generally a popular Bangkok travel month; reserve a gallery slot ahead.
gettingThere: Address: 111 Soi Sukhumvit 40, Phra Khanong, Khlong Toei. BTS Ekkamai is about an 18–20-minute walk (official pages differ slightly); a taxi or ride-hail to “Dib Bangkok” avoids the walk. Limited basement parking and a separate parking building five minutes away are listed by the museum; visitors get up to three hours free parking.
booking: Advance online booking is recommended; the museum says walk-ins are possible but availability is not guaranteed. Payment on site is by credit card or bank transfer, no cash. Reserve the separate Straight Up Sunset Light Program independently. Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable per the FAQ.
accessibility: Officially listed: accessible basement parking, elevators and wheelchairs on request; disability admission is THB 150. Confirm route/access needs with the museum before visiting, since detailed gallery access information is not specified on the visit page.
practicalTips: Check the official What’s On page close to travel: the known Giving Life run ends 3 May 2027, but December opening hours and any later programme may change.
Bring a payment card or arrange bank transfer; cash is not accepted for on-site tickets.
Under-12s must be accompanied by an adult; all gallery visitors must be at least seven.
The bistro and shop can be visited without an exhibition ticket.
decemberNotes: Giving Life is scheduled through 3 May 2027, so it should be showing in December 2026. The first Chanel Gateway Commission, Project 147, is reported on view within the exhibition through 5 May 2027. These are published end dates, not a guarantee against programme changes. December 2026 holiday hours and any later special events are not yet confirmed.
uncertainties: December 2026 holiday closures, special events and any later exhibition changes are not confirmed; recheck the official calendar.
Exact visit time is subjective; 2–3 hours is a planning estimate.
The visit page says Ekkamai is a 20-minute walk while the home page says 18 minutes.
The linked building photo depicts the museum as photographed for Wallpaper* in 2025, not its December 2026 exhibition.
